reviews.text:
My beloved dog had lost his appetite, so I took him to the vet as a precaution. He died three hours after being left at this hospital.

I inquired about what happened after he was left there.

I believe it was because they performed blood tests, IV fluids, and other tests on him while he was weak.

The hospital staff may have been doing their best.

He was fine just yesterday... Thinking about that, I can't help but write this down.

I think my dog ​​would want me to be smiling and not crying, so I'll stop here.
While I was in the waiting room, I heard someone who seemed to be the head doctor shouting, which made me feel very uncomfortable.

The doctors and nurses are incredibly kind, and I truly rely on them.

They hardly ever take days off, so they're always able to respond to sudden illnesses, which is why I always use their services.

They also provide thorough health checkups.

My dog ​​ate a sock that had fallen on the ground during our walk, and we rushed him to the vet 15 minutes later. As soon as we arrived, we left him in the examination room, and after more than an hour we were called in. I naturally assumed they would have treated him by now, but they hadn't done anything. The doctor asked me some questions and gave me an explanation, saying that treatment would follow. I understand that there is a queue for consultations, but I have doubts about their handling of an emergency. On top of that, they made a mistake with the bill, charging me about 5000 yen more than necessary, and at the end, the receptionist said, "We are sorry for keeping you waiting today." I don't mind waiting since it's not an appointment system, but I'm not satisfied with their handling of the situation, and they seemed completely clueless. I'm going to a different vet.

Thank you for your continued support.

It gets quite crowded on weekends, and the waiting room isn't very spacious, so it gets very packed.

I've used the pet hotel several times, but the last time my pet was found with feces stuck to its bottom. I was surprised and saddened, as I've always had a very positive impression of your care.

I still want to go to the vet, but I've decided not to use the pet hotel anymore.

My dog ​​was being treated by Dr. Inoue, but on the day his condition suddenly worsened, the hospital director and a resident (a recently hired veterinarian?) took care of my dog. I went to see him in the morning and asked them to keep him alive, but after I left him in their care, I received a call two hours later saying that even though he was still connected to a ventilator and his overall condition was poor, they had removed the ventilator because he was breathing on his own. They didn't check how long he was able to breathe on his own. Then he stopped breathing and they were now performing CPR. I received the call asking if I could come now, and shortly after that, my beloved dog passed away. I don't know the circumstances under which they removed the ventilator without consulting the owner, and anyone should know that an animal connected to a ventilator can't breathe on its own. Why did they make that decision? Why didn't they consult the owner? If this were a human, it would be an act of murder that goes against medical practice. As I stood there crying in front of my dog's corpse, the hospital director smiled and said, "He did so well." The fact that they could act in that manner in front of the grieving owner, and the reason for removing the ventilator remains unclear, is unacceptable behavior for someone entrusted with a life, both as a person and as a veterinarian. I won't go into further explanation as the life can't be brought back, but I understand that everything was irresponsible and showed no empathy for the animal's life or the owner's feelings. I can't process my feelings.

Please give me back my dog's life.

Dr. Inoue called and apologized along with explaining the situation.

I sincerely hope that no one else becomes a victim.
My beloved dog, who passed away, received excellent care from you. And now my second dog is also receiving your services.

We always rely on the vice-director for our care.

We adopted two dogs together, so we visited quite frequently when they were puppies. They're already 8 years old, but yesterday our dachshund suddenly couldn't stand up, so we went to a nearby hospital. They diagnosed it as a leg injury, not a herniated disc, but we were a little skeptical, so we got a second opinion. He was diagnosed with a stage 1 herniated disc, and I (who also have a herniated disc) was prescribed the same medication and told to rest for two weeks. I'm glad we got him checked before the symptoms worsened.

I think it would be quite difficult to go to any hospital without pet insurance, so I don't mind that.

The staff are all very kind and gentle, so our dogs are able to visit calmly. However, the waiting room is small and faces each other, so our dogs tend to bark at larger dogs, hence the minus one star!

There are many reviews, but there are many animal hospitals and many veterinarians. I hope you can find a veterinarian you can trust to take care of your sick dog or cat.

It's open year-round and the hospital is clean. I haven't had the opportunity to get a groomer or shampoo, so I can't comment on the pros or cons, but you'll receive a postcard with discounted health checkups near your pet's birthday. However, I wholeheartedly recommend not visiting for treatment of an illness or injury.
If an abnormality is found during a health checkup, I recommend immediately taking the test results to another hospital.
Both doctors are gentle, but I felt they were very uninformed when it comes to cats. Although the testing facilities are well-equipped, accurate diagnoses are not provided, so I don't recommend seeking a second opinion at this hospital.
When my cat was unwell, I had my blood tested almost weekly, but the cause was never determined. I don't understand why they would take such a burden and require weekly blood tests. The diagnosis results seemed to be a case of insurance, listing only various possibilities and deliberately avoiding a specific diagnosis.
I was kicked out of the examination room when blood was taken, and I've never seen them listening to, palpating, or taking a temperature in front of the owner. I remember being surprised when I asked for an explanation about the prescribed medication and was told something along the lines of, "They're busy and will send someone else to do it."
Also, even though he was a cat, his vaccinations were given between the shoulder blades. When he swelled up, I regretted not being able to stop them as his owner. I took him to the doctor immediately after the swelling occurred, but was told, "I've never seen anything like this before; it's rare." I panicked and went to another hospital for a second opinion. I learned there that the location of the vaccine is important, as cats can develop malignant tumors in the area where the vaccine is given, and all the doctors at each hospital were very surprised that the vaccine was given between the shoulder blades. In the end, the swelling went down and it didn't become a major problem, but it was a deciding factor that made me realize that I couldn't trust him as a veterinarian.
He tried a lot of things, but I will never use his services again.
